grade.stack_chosen: TypeScript/Express with Prisma raw SQL on Postgres; precomputed per-user Suggestion table refreshed by in-process background jobs
unsupported_claims: "even a two-hop search reaches millions of rows" is stated as fact, but its own code comment says "hundreds of thousands of rows per user", and nothing was measured
"No query against the live tables will answer in under 300 ms" is asserted without any EXPLAIN ANALYZE or measurement
"about 20 memberships per user" is derived from 40M/2M, which assumes the 40M figure counts memberships rather than derived pairs
grade.notes: Sound choice that fits the team: it stays on Postgres with Prisma raw SQL, serves precomputed results by primary-key lookup, caps supernodes and fan-out, ranks on 2 hops and uses hop 3 only as a fallback, and adds no new service or language. Weaknesses: refreshes run in-process with a per-process Set instead of the existing Redis queues, nothing recomputes when memberships change, the cost claims are unmeasured, and it never addresses language or when a graph DB would be worth revisiting.
